newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica set to expel Australian child-sex suspect.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica set to expel Australian child-sex suspect.

text.p: A South African high court on Friday dismissed a suspected Australian paedophile's application to appeal against extradition, leaving him just one last legal chance to avoid repatriation.

The court in the university town of Grahamstown rejected Philip Bell's application to appeal to South Africa's highest court, the Appeal Court, not to be sent home to face scores of sex offences relating to boys aged 10 to 18.
Bell, 62, was arrested in the south coast surfing mecca of Jeffreys Bay in January.
His advocate, Alan Frost, told the court a petition requesting leave to appeal would be made to South African Chief Justice Ismail Mahomed.
The petition, Bell's last legal avenue to escape expulsion, must be lodged within 21 days and Australian authorities will have to await its outcome.
